c.tagline: Benin's quiet official capital of royal palaces, Vodun heritage, and lagoon calm, overshadowed by bustling Cotonou.

taxi.fareNote: Almost all rides are by zemidjan (motorcycle taxi) or shared taxi with no meters; agree on the price in CFA francs before setting off.

emergency.note: 118 reaches the fire brigade; response times can be slow outside the city center, so hotels and clinics are often the fastest first call.

avoid.reason: Petty theft can occur around Ouando and Grand Marché market areas; avoid zémidjan motorbike-taxi rides late at night.

hood_desc: Home to the National Assembly and the Ethnographic Museum's Yoruba masks and royal artifacts; the natural first stop for understanding Beninese and Yoruba history.
A leafy colonial-era plaza with a statue of Porto-Novo's first king, ringed by administrative buildings; a calm spot to get oriented near the center.
The historic royal quarter around King Toffa's Palace (Honmé Museum), on UNESCO's tentative list; suits travelers focused on Beninese royal and Vodun heritage.
A quiet residential district built by returning Afro-Brazilian former slaves, known for Portuguese-style facades and the Da Silva Museum of Beninese-Brazilian history.
The working port and market district on the lagoon, where canoes and zemidjans converge around Porto-Novo's largest market; best for travelers wanting an authentic, unpolished feel.

water.note: Stick to bottled or treated water throughout Benin.

transit.hours: No fixed schedule; zemidjans and shared taxis run informally from early morning to late evening, thinning out after dark.
transit.pay: Cash only (CFA francs), negotiated per ride before departing; there is no fare card or ticketing system.
transit.note: Porto-Novo has no formal public transit network. Zemidjans (motorcycle taxis) are the main way to get around the city, supplemented by shared taxis and bush taxis to Cotonou and other towns; canoes still cross the lagoon to nearby villages.

bus: Shared taxis/bush taxis to Cotonou and regional towns
ferry: Lagoon canoe (pirogue) crossings to nearby lakeside villages

tip.r: Not part of local custom; rounding up small amounts is appreciated at tourist-oriented restaurants and hotels but never expected.
